assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors fuse a deaminase to a Cas9 nickase to make defined C-to-T and A-to-G changes without double-strand breaks, turning a nucleic-acid chemical reaction (cytidine and adenosine deamination, with engineered TadA acting on DNA) into a general programmable tool. Strongly original, clear, and already clinical.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the conceptual and engineering work; Komor (cytosine base editor) and Gaudelli (adenine base editor) were decisive trainees. A single-laureate prize is plausible, but a Liu plus trainee configuration is arguable; I propose Liu alone, keeping the third slot open for other candidates.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced widely, with first therapeutic uses in patients. Timely, though recognition of CRISPR in 2020 means the committee may regard this as a downstream extension.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views base editing as sufficiently distinct from the 2020 CRISPR-Cas9 prize.
Whether credit should include Komor and Gaudelli; I cannot verify the allocation myself.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Chemically induced proximity to hijack the ubiquitin-proteasome system for degradation of target proteins. It converts a biological process into a designable chemical principle (bifunctional degraders, molecular glues acting via cereblon and related ligases) and has produced a new drug modality in clinical trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated PROTACs; Ciulli provided the structure-guided VHL-based degraders that made the approach drug-like. The thalidomide-cereblon discovery (Handa, Ito) is a separate strand that complicates a three-person split.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation across many groups and many clinical programs, though approvals are not yet established, so timing is arguably slightly early.
uncertainties: Allocation between PROTAC and molecular-glue/cereblon strands is unresolved.
No approved degrader drug yet, as far as I know; I have not verified this.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading nucleotides electrically as single molecules pass through a protein pore is a fundamental analytical idea realized in long-read sequencing. It also enables direct detection of modified bases and nucleotide analytes, which matters to my own field of nucleotide chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Brandon, Branton and Deamer demonstrated polynucleotide translocation (1996); Bayley engineered the pore, and Akeson demonstrated strand control and base discrimination. Credit is spread over at least five people, so fair trio selection is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Technology is mature and independently validated, and widely used for genomes and RNA modifications. Recognition timely.
uncertainties: Choice of three among five contributors is contentious.
The relative roles of pore engineering and motor-enzyme control are hard to weigh.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates reframe how cells organize biochemistry without membranes. The impact is broad, covering nucleolus, stress granules and signalling, and it connects physical chemistry with cell biology.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne published the foundational 2009 P-granule work; Rosen contributed the multivalent-interaction phase-transition framework, and Pappu and Mittag the sequence-grammar physics. Credit is plausible for a trio but contested.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly growing, but many in vivo claims are still debated, with concerns about artefacts from overexpression and about whether condensates truly have functional roles. As an experimentalist I want stricter quantitative validation.
uncertainties: Is the discovery chemistry, or more properly biology or physics?

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shokat's tethering approach revealed a cryptic switch-II pocket in KRAS G12C and enabled covalent inhibitors that overturned the view that KRAS is undruggable. Also earlier chemical-genetic analogue-sensitive kinase work. A clear case of chemistry opening a biological target class.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is cleanly to a single person for the covalent KRAS strategy, though Amgen and Mirati teams carried out drug development.
assessment.maturity: Sotorasib and adagrasib have been approved and the mechanism has been confirmed by many independent groups. Timely.
uncertainties: The prize might need to be shared with other contributions, for example the analogue-sensitive kinase work, which is a separate strand.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative proteomics by mass spectrometry made large-scale measurement of proteins, modifications and interactions routine, much as I rely on LC-MS/MS for nucleotide pool quantification. The impact is foundational for biochemistry and medicine.
assessment.attribution: Mann, Aebersold and Yates are central (shotgun proteomics, SRM and quantification, SILAC). Gygi, Hunt and Heck are also major, so a three-person cut leaves out meritorious contributors.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently validated for 20 or more years; the ESI/MALDI precedent in 2002 means the committee may think this has been partly recognized.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 prize in mass spectrometry for biomolecules.
Hard to separate the contribution of several leaders.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs allow site-specific incorporation of unnatural amino acids into proteins in living cells, giving chemists direct control of protein chemistry in vivo. Original, general and widely used.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first in vivo systems; Chin expanded to quadruplet codons, orthogonal ribosomes and multiple-site recoding. Yokoyama and Mehl are also credited, adding contention.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced, used widely, though therapeutic and industrial impacts are still developing.
uncertainties: Mehl and Yokoyama contributions may deserve recognition.
Whether the ongoing recoding work is mature enough.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase catalyzes N2 reduction with one of the most complex metallocofactors; structures of the FeMo cofactor with its central carbide and of the turnover states explain the chemistry of biological nitrogen fixation. Fundamental enzymology of great scale.
assessment.attribution: Rees led the structural work (including the interstitial carbide with Einsle), while Dean and Seefeldt contributed genetics and mechanism, and Ribbe the cofactor biosynthesis. Fair credit is hard.
assessment.maturity: Structural picture is mature, but the actual catalytic mechanism (E4 state, hydride chemistry) is still debated, so the interpretation is not fully stable.
uncertainties: Mechanism of N2 reduction is not settled.
Attribution among structural, genetic and spectroscopic contributors is unresolved.
